The Cuyahoga County Medical Examiner Office determined that seven people in Cuyahoga County died from exposure during the first half of February due to the combination of cold weather and inadequate housing with proper heating. Temperatures during the first half of February were largely below freezing with many nights with lows in the single digits and wind chills below zero.

The Eagle Creek watershed received an average of 1.50 of rainfall on Sunday the 9th between 6 am and early afternoon. The runoff resulted in moderate flooding as indicated by the USGS river gage which crested at 11.0 feet on the morning of the 10th. The flood waters inundated Brookside Road, 6th Street, Eagle Creek Park, and Firestine Park. Approximately two dozen Homes along Brookside road were surrounded and inaccessible and experienced basement flooding.

Rainfall amounts averaging 1.50 fell over the Blanchard watershed on Sunday the 9th. This resulted in minor flooding in the City of Findlay. The USGS river gage at Findlay registered a crest of 12.4 feet on the morning of the 11th. Flooding impacted areas near Riverside Park and East Main Cross Street in the City of Findlay. Flooding on County Road 223 and portions of Howard Street. Water approached some properties on Liberty Street and Apple Alley. East Main Cross Street flooded under the Osborne Bridge. Minor flooding of a golf course near Country Club Drive.

Moderate rainfall averaging 1.50 fell over the Lye Creek watershed. This resulted in minor flooding along County Road 180 or Bright Road flooded to State Route 37, just south of East Sandusky Street. The USGS river gage crested at 7.0 feet during the evening of the 9th.

Minor flooding along the Black Fork of the Mohican River at Shelby occurred on May 9 after nearly 3 inches of rain fell in the watershed. The flood waters reached the Main Street bridge. Shelby is split in half when the Black Fork spills onto Main Street at a stage of 16.5 feet. The USGS river gage at Shelby reached a crest of 16.2 feet on the early evening of the 9th. Minor flooding impacted the athletic fields and there was some property damage. A portion of Seltzer Park, back roads and low-lying areas were flooded.

An average of two inches of rain fell over Wyandot County and the Tymochtee Creek on May 9th resulting in minor flooding. The USGS river gage at Crawford reported a crest of 8.5 feet on the 11th. The relatively flat land and slow runoff displaced the flooding to nearly 24 hours after the rain ended over the area. Numerous County Highways were flooded including CH 16 flooded east of State Route 53 north of Tymotchee. Other County Highways that were inundated include CH 35, 4, 16, 37, 38, 42, 47, and 53.

Moderate rainfall fell over the Mohican Valley on Sunday May 9th. Rainfall amounts between 2 to 3 inches was reported between 6 am and 6 pm. The Black Fork reported flooding from well upstream in Richland County and again down in Loudonville where it meets the Mohican River. The Black Fork USGS gage at Loudonville exceeded flood stage on Sunday afternoon and reached moderate flood stage on the morning of the 10th, cresting at 11.3 feet. Flood waters inundated recreational campgrounds and liveries along the river. Due to the early season timing, there was limited population along the river, however damage was reported to numerous campers and some permanent structures.
High water road closure on State Route 529  near Cardington, could have been related to Whetstone Creek overflow.
High water road closure on State Route 529 and 61 between Fulton and Mt. Gilead.

Rainfall of 1.5 inch averaged across the Portage River watershed on May 9th cause minor flooding in Pemberville. Water was in the backyard of residents on Bierley, Bridge, and Water Streets in Pemberville.  The USGS river gage at Woodville reported a river stage of 10.1 feet on the 10th.
The Sandusky River at Tiffin came out of banks on the 11th and encroached on school property south of town and some private properties north of town. Some minor road inundation also occurred.

Moderate rainfall over 1.5 inches across the Nimishillen watershed led to minor flooding along the creek and several tributaries in Stark County.  In North Industry some minor flooding caused low lying portions of Southeast Sparta Avenue and Allenford Drive. Flood waters inundated recreational fields of Canton South High School. Water backed up into a mobile home park on Cleveland Southwest Avenue in Canton Township. The USGS river gauge in North Industry recorded a stage of 11.4 feet.
Roads inundated include High Street, Larue Prospect Road, School Street, and parts of Vine Street. USGS river gage crested at 13.0 feet.

Minor flooding in Prospect from the Scioto River which reached 11.9 feet on the 12th based on the USGS river gage. Main impacts were to Winter Street and SR 203 north of town.

A tornado touched down in eastern Lucas County about a mile north of Curtice near the intersection of North Curtice Road and State Route 2.  The tornado traveled northeast for about five miles and lifted near Reno Beach.  The damage path was intermittent and no more than 35 yards in width.  Several camping trailers were overturned by the tornado and a large sign was blown down. Dozens of trees were toppled along the damage path.
Penny sized hail was observed.

Pockets of downed trees were observed in several locations just to the north of the Turnpike. A large dust devil formed near a ball field at Champion High School.  Witnesses estimated that the dust devil was as least 40 feet tall and on the ground for a couple hundred yards.  The dust devil lifted a baby carriage over twenty feet in the air, threw an equipment bag on to the roof of the schools gymnasium and tossed several sheets of plywood.  No injuries were reported.

Intense bands of lake effect snow prompted several vehicle accidents on interstate highways in Cuyahoga County during the late morning hours of the 1st. The largest vehicle accident was on Interstate 90 in Rocky River, where 12 to 15 cars were involved in an accident near Hilliard Road and additional cars crashed further west due to stopped traffic and poor road conditions. Additional accidents were reported on Interstates 480, 71, 77 and 271 within the county. No injuries were reported with any of these incidents. Isolated snow totals of up to 6 inches were reported in Parma and North Royalton, but much of the county saw 4 inches or less of snow.

In Cuyahoga County, rain changed completely over to snow between 9 and 11 PM on April 20. Snow ramped up in intensity just after midnight with periods of quarter to half mile visibility in snow at Cleveland Hopkins Airport. Once the event was over, snow varied greatly across the county with areas nearest Lake Erie receiving less than an inch of snow to 5 to 7 inches in many of the southern and eastern suburbs of Cleveland. The highest measured snowfall total was 7.5 inches by a CoCoRaHS observer in Shaker Heights. Other totals in the county include: 7.1 inches in Parma, 6.8 inches in Chagrin Falls, 6.1 inches in Lyndhurst, 5.5 inches in Seven Hills, Strongsville, North Royalton, and Cleveland Heights, and 5.1 inches in South Euclid. Communities near Lake Erie received one inch of snow or less with one half inch reported in both Euclid and Lakewood.

In Geauga County, rain changed completely over to snow between 9 and 11 PM on April 20. Snow ramped up in intensity just after midnight with periods of quarter to half mile visibility in snow. Once the event was over, snow ranged from 5 to 7 inches across the county. The highest measured snowfall total was 7 inches by several snow spotters across the county in Hambden Township, Chardon, and Thompson Township. Other totals in the county include: 6.4 inches in Montville, 6 inches in South Russell, and 5 inches in Burton.

Intense bands of lake effect snow prompted several vehicle accidents on Interstate 77 in northern Summit County during the late morning hours of the 1st. A total of 9 multi-vehicle accidents occurred on Interstate 77 in Richfield and Bath Township with a total of 23 vehicles involved. Of the 42 occupants of the vehicles, 6 were transported to area hospitals with non-life-threatening injuries. Interstate 77 was closed from the Cuyahoga/Summit County border to the Ghent Road exit for several hours.

Above normal temperatures in March and above normal to record high temperatures in early April in Northwest Pennsylvania allowed for area fruit crops to begin budding ahead of schedule in April. A low pressure system brought several rounds of snow to the region on April 20-21 and residual snow allowed for temperatures to cool considerably with low temperatures in the upper 20s to lower 30s into the morning of the 22nd. For area farmers, the combination of snow and cold damaged area grape crops in interior portions of Erie County, Pennsylvania. The area with the most damage was in portions of Harborcreek and North East Townships near Interstate 90. These vineyards were heavily damaged with an estimated 85 to 95% crop loss on the first shoots of grapes. In some areas, some of these first shoots were only slightly damaged but the second shoots of grapes were delayed after an unimpressive first batch of grapes. Local news reports relay that some of the area will have only half a grape crop for the year. Area apple and cherry crops were also damaged prompting smaller yields.

A push of colder air across the Great Lakes region in early December allowed for lake effect snow to develop. Lake effect snow showers off Lake Michigan moved east into the Lake Erie region and became organized into a single banded lake effect snow event that impacted portions of Northeast Ohio. This band developed around 5 PM on December 6th and increased in intensity over the next several hours. Snowfall rates just after midnight were in excess of one inch per hour and there were social media reports of thundersnow in the area. Snowfall tapered off quickly on December 7th, effectively ending by 5 AM. The hardest hit county during the event was the interior portion of Ashtabula County, south of Interstate 90. A trained snow spotter in Monroe Township reported 9 inches of new snow near daybreak. Other snowfall reports in Ashtabula County include 7.2 inches of snow in Jefferson, 7 inches of snow in Kelloggsville, 3.8 inches of snow in Pierpont, and 3.5 inches of snow in Harpersfield Township. Impacts across the area were minimal given the timing and low density of snow, but slow downs on Interstate 90 were briefly noted.

The ASOS at Findlay Airport measured a 52 knot (60 mph) wind gust at 2:02 pm. Around this same time, a power pole snapped, blocking portions of Township Road 205, east of the city of Findlay. Numerous power outages were reported in Hancock County due to the winds downing power lines.
A social media report and photo showed the door of a small outbuilding was blown off due to the wind.

The ASOS at Toledo Express Airport measured a 54 knot (62 mph) wind gust at 10:27 am. Many trees and power lines were downed across the county due to winds. Local broadcast media reported a tree was downed onto a vehicle in the Sylvania area. Power outages across the county reached up to 29,500 customers.
There were many reports of trees down across the county, including Bradner, Luckey, and Weston. Numerous power outages were reported across the county.
An AWOS in Port Clinton measured a 61 mph wind gust at 12:55 PM. A trained spotter east of Clay Center measured a 60 mph wind gust around Noon.
Five power poles were completely broken off near the ground on Ohio State Route 510 north of Clyde.
Sandusky Fire Department reported a roof had blown off a commercial building on the south side of Sandusky. A trained weather spotter measured a 58 mph wind gust at 1:25 pm.
Wind gusts caused portions of a roof of a police sub station to be damaged in Lorain. Trees were downed around the county. The ASOS at Lorain County Airport reported a 56 mph wind gust at 2:23 PM.

A trained spotter in Parma with well sited wind equipment measured a 56 knot (64 mph) wind gust at 3:15 pm. ASOS locations at Cleveland Hopkins Airport and Burke Lakefront Airport each measured 59 mph wind gusts during the afternoon hours on the 11th. Several trees and light poles were downed in the county, especially the southwestern portions of the county, including North Olmsted and Berea. One of these trees fell onto a house near the intersection of Gessner and Walter Roads. Over 19,000 customers were without power in the county.

A tree fell on a car driving on Old French Road during the afternoon hours of the 11th. The driver was not injured. Winds gusted as high as 64 mph, which was recorded at Erie International Airport at 4:43 pm. Winds through the afternoon caused numerous trees to fall across the area including Millcreek Township, Girard Township, and Harborcreek. A large tree fell on a house near 4th and Pennsylvania in Erie. Two homes were damaged by trees on West 9th Street in Erie. At least 4 cars were hit by falling trees during the afternoon hours. In Harborcreek, a vehicle crashed into a fallen tree on Route 5, but no injuries were reported.
Trumbull County Sheriff Dispatch reported a tree down in the Cortland Area and another in the Kinsman area from thunderstorms early on the 11th.
